questions.q: What did the comparison of exam marks show?
options: The difference was not decisive but was disturbing.
The difference was too small to be measured.
Quiet halls produced clearly better marks.
questions.explain: not large enough to settle the argument — but it was large enough to unsettle it：不足以定论，却足以让人不安。

questions.q: What happened to students told their results were provisional?
options: They performed better in the following term.
They asked to retake the exam.
questions.explain: students who had been told their results were provisional went on to outperform their peers in the following term.

questions.q: What does the last sentence imply about exams?
options: Exam results can influence the very ability they claim to measure.
questions.explain: 末句 helping to produce it：分数不仅「测量」知识，还反过来「制造/影响」了被测量的东西（后续努力）。

questions.q: Which word best describes the researchers' position?
questions.explain: The researchers are careful to say that a label is not a destiny：措辞审慎，拒绝过度推论。

reading.title: The Price of Cleaner Air
reading.passage: Few policies are as easy to praise and as hard to price as air quality regulation. A factory ordered to fit cleaner equipment faces a bill it can count; the benefit — fewer hospital visits across a region — is spread thinly over thousands of households and years, and therefore rarely appears in anyone's accounts. Economists have tried to close this gap by putting a number on avoided illness, but such figures are routinely attacked as speculative. The objection is not unreasonable, yet it is applied asymmetrically: the cost of compliance is treated as hard fact, while the cost of doing nothing is treated as guesswork. Several long-term studies now suggest that the latter has been consistently underestimated. If so, the familiar complaint that regulation is too expensive may rest less on arithmetic than on which column of the ledger we are willing to look at.

questions.q: Why is the benefit of cleaner air hard to account for?
options: It is spread over many households and years.
questions.explain: the benefit … is spread thinly over thousands of households and years, and therefore rarely appears in anyone's accounts.

questions.q: What does "applied asymmetrically" refer to?
options: Both sides use the same data.
Costs and benefits are judged by different standards.
questions.explain: 合规成本被当作 hard fact，而不作为的代价被当作 guesswork——同一把尺子没有用在两边，即标准不对称。

questions.q: What do several long-term studies suggest?
options: Air quality has no effect on health.
The cost of compliance has been exaggerated.
The cost of inaction has been underestimated.
questions.explain: Several long-term studies now suggest that the latter has been consistently underestimated（后者＝不作为的代价，被低估）。

questions.q: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Claims that regulation is too costly may reflect accounting bias.
questions.explain: 末句点题：所谓「监管太贵」，更多取决于我们愿意看账本的哪一栏，即核算口径的偏差。

reading.title: The Myth of the Empty Mind
reading.passage: We tend to assume that doing nothing is the absence of thought. Brain-imaging studies have made that assumption increasingly difficult to hold. When participants are left alone in a quiet room with no task, a network associated with memory, planning and self-reference becomes more, not less, active. Far from idling, the mind rehearses recent conversations, simulates tomorrow's difficulties and quietly rearranges what it knows. This may explain why solutions so often arrive in the shower rather than at the desk. It also complicates a familiar complaint about modern work: that constant interruption is merely a loss of time. If uninterrupted stretches are when the brain consolidates and recombines, then a calendar packed with short meetings is not only inefficient; it removes the very condition under which understanding forms. Rest, on this account, is not the reward for thinking but part of the machinery of it.

questions.q: What have brain-imaging studies shown about a person left with no task?
options: A network linked to memory and planning becomes more active.
Only visual areas of the brain respond.
The brain cannot be measured reliably.
questions.explain: a network associated with memory, planning and self-reference becomes more, not less, active.

questions.q: Why does the author mention solutions arriving in the shower?
options: To show that people think better when relaxed
To argue that showers save time
To introduce a new imaging technique
questions.explain: 「远非空转」的大脑会排演、模拟、重组已知，故答案常在淋浴时冒出——用以说明放松时思维仍在运作。

questions.q: What does the author suggest about a calendar full of short meetings?
options: It is the most efficient way to work.
It removes the condition needed for understanding to form.
It has no effect on how people think.
questions.explain: it removes the very condition under which understanding forms（恰恰剥夺了理解得以形成的条件）。

questions.q: What does the last sentence mean?
options: Thinking is impossible without a desk.
Rest should be earned by hard work.
Rest is a component of thinking itself.
questions.explain: Rest … is not the reward for thinking but part of the machinery of it：休息不是思考之后的奖赏，而是思考机制本身的一环。

reading.title: What a Dictionary Leaves Out
reading.passage: A dictionary tells us what a word may mean; it is remarkably silent on what a word has been allowed to mean. Consider the vocabulary of work. For much of the last century, terms such as "career" and "profession" were reserved for occupations that required formal qualifications, while the activities that filled most people's days were described with humbler verbs. The distinction was presented as neutral, a matter of precision. Yet it quietly sorted lives into those that progressed and those that merely passed. Linguists point out that such boundaries rarely survive contact with evidence: the skills required in so-called unskilled work often take years to acquire. What is interesting is not that the labels were unfair — that is easily said — but that they were so durable. A category, once printed, acquires the quiet authority of something that was always there; challenging it requires not a better definition but a willingness to notice that a definition was made at all.

questions.q: According to the passage, how were "career" and "profession" once used?
options: Only for work needing formal qualifications
questions.explain: terms such as career and profession were reserved for occupations that required formal qualifications.

questions.q: What does the author find most interesting about such labels?
questions.explain: What is interesting is not that the labels were unfair — that is easily said — but that they were so durable（耐人寻味的是其持久性）。

questions.q: What does "a category, once printed, acquires the quiet authority of something that was always there" suggest?
options: Written labels come to seem natural and unquestionable.
Old words are more precise than new ones.
questions.explain: 一旦被印成条目，分类就获得了「仿佛向来如此」的隐蔽权威——即被自然化、不再被质疑。

questions.q: Which statement would the author most likely agree with?
options: We should notice that definitions are human constructions.
Definitions are discovered rather than made.
Better dictionaries will solve the problem.
questions.explain: 末句：challenging it requires … a willingness to notice that a definition was made at all（意识到定义是被造出来的）。

reading.title: The Tool That Changed the Task
reading.passage: When a new automation tool was introduced into a hospital's records department, managers expected it to reduce headcount. Eighteen months later, staff numbers were unchanged, but the work was unrecognisable. Clerks who had spent their days transcribing forms now spent them checking the tool's output, handling the cases it flagged as uncertain, and explaining decisions to patients. The tool had not removed the job; it had relocated its difficulty to the edges, where judgement was still required. Researchers who studied the change call this the "residual problem": automation reliably handles the routine middle and leaves behind precisely those cases that are hardest to codify. The consequence is counter-intuitive. Because the remaining work is less repetitive, it demands more experience, not less — and the people doing it need support and training that the original plan had not budgeted for. Efficiency, it turns out, is not the same as simplification.

questions.q: What did managers expect the automation tool to do?
questions.explain: managers expected it to reduce headcount（缩减人员编制）。

questions.q: What happened to the clerks' work after eighteen months?
options: It was moved to another department.
It shifted to checking, judging and explaining.
questions.explain: checking the tool's output, handling the cases it flagged as uncertain, and explaining decisions to patients.

questions.q: What does the "residual problem" refer to?
options: The difficult cases automation leaves behind
The high cost of the software
Staff refusing to use new tools
questions.explain: automation reliably handles the routine middle and leaves behind precisely those cases that are hardest to codify.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Automation can make the remaining work more demanding.
Clerks need fewer skills than before.
questions.explain: 末两句点题：剩余工作更不重复、更需要经验，Efficiency … is not the same as simplification（效率≠简化）。

reading.title: The Empty Lot
reading.passage: There was a piece of empty land behind our apartment block. For years people used it as a car park, and nobody thought much about it. Last spring a few neighbours asked the owners if they could turn part of it into a garden. To everyone's surprise, the owners agreed. Within two months there were twelve wooden boxes of soil, a water tap and a small tool shed. Families each took one box. Children planted beans and tomatoes; older residents grew flowers. Nobody was paid, and the tools were bought with money collected door to door. By autumn the corner had become the busiest place in the block. People who had lived there for ten years and never spoken now met every Saturday morning. The owners have since said the garden can stay.

questions.q: What was the empty land used for before last spring?
questions.explain: 第一句之后：For years people used it as a car park（多年来被当作停车场）。

questions.q: How was the garden paid for?
questions.explain: the tools were bought with money collected door to door（挨家挨户凑钱买的）。

questions.q: What is the main change the garden brought?
options: Neighbours began to know one another.
questions.explain: 倒数第二句：住了十年都没说过话的邻居现在每周六早上见面——花园带来的是邻里关系的改变。

reading.title: Bikes on Campus
reading.passage: Our university started a bike-sharing scheme last September. Five hundred bicycles were placed near the gates, the library and the dining halls. Students unlock them with a phone app and pay by the minute. At first the scheme was so popular that there were never enough bikes at eight in the morning. The office then moved one hundred bicycles from the quieter west gate to the teaching area. It also added painted parking lines, because bikes left across the path had become a problem. Six months later, the number of short bus trips inside the campus had fallen by a third. Some students still complain that the app fails in the rain, and a few older teachers say they would rather walk. But most agree that getting from the dormitory to a lecture now takes half the time.

questions.q: What problem did the office face at first?
options: There were not enough bikes in the morning.
questions.explain: there were never enough bikes at eight in the morning（早上八点车总是不够）。

questions.q: Why were painted parking lines added?
options: To make the campus look nicer
Because the app could not find bikes
questions.explain: because bikes left across the path had become a problem（自行车横放在路上成了问题）。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the last paragraph?
options: Most users think the scheme saves time.
The scheme has been given up.
Older teachers use the app most.
questions.explain: most agree that getting from the dormitory to a lecture now takes half the time（多数人认为路程时间减半）。

reading.title: Breakfast Before Class
reading.passage: A primary school in the north of the city began offering a free breakfast at half past seven. The idea came from a teacher who noticed that several children arrived tired and could not concentrate until mid-morning. The meal is simple: porridge, an egg, milk and a piece of fruit. No one is asked to sign up, and no child is marked out as poor, because everyone eats together in the same hall. After one term, teachers reported fewer visits to the school nurse in the morning and better attention in the first lesson. Parents were more surprised than anyone. Many said their children now left home earlier without being asked. The head teacher admits the scheme costs money, but she points out that it is far cheaper than repeating a year of teaching.

questions.q: Why did the school start the breakfast scheme?
options: Parents asked for a longer school day.
Some children were too tired to concentrate in the morning.
questions.explain: a teacher who noticed that several children arrived tired and could not concentrate until mid-morning.

questions.q: Why is no child marked out as poor?
options: Because the food is free for teachers too
Because everyone eats together in the same hall
Because the school does not keep records
Because only a few children come
questions.explain: because everyone eats together in the same hall（所有人同厅就餐，不区分谁需要帮助）。

questions.q: What does the head teacher suggest about the cost?
options: It is too high to continue.
It is small compared with the cost of children falling behind.
It will be covered by the nurse.
questions.explain: far cheaper than repeating a year of teaching（比留级重读一年便宜得多）。

reading.title: The Box by the Gate
reading.passage: At the end of our street there is a wooden box on a post, with a glass door and a painted sign: take a book, leave a book. A retired teacher built it three years ago from an old cupboard. It has no lock, no membership and no opening hours. Anyone can walk up, open the door and choose whatever is inside. At first there were only a dozen books, mostly dictionaries. Now the box holds novels, cookbooks, children's picture books and even a few textbooks. Neighbours say the rule works better than they expected: people rarely take without leaving something, and the box has never been damaged. The teacher's only complaint is that she has to straighten the books every few days. Last winter the council put a small roof over the box to keep the rain out. It is, she says, the cheapest library in town.

questions.q: What is the rule of the wooden box?
options: Take a book, leave a book
Borrow and return within two weeks
questions.explain: 牌子上写着 take a book, leave a book（拿一本，留一本）。

questions.q: What surprised the neighbours?
options: The teacher closed it in winter.
The box was never damaged and people follow the rule.
questions.explain: people rarely take without leaving something, and the box has never been damaged.

questions.q: What does "the cheapest library in town" suggest?
options: The books are of low quality.
It is smaller than other libraries.
It costs almost nothing to run.
questions.explain: 无锁、无会员、无开放时间、由旧柜子改造、只加了个小屋顶——运行成本几乎为零，故称最便宜的图书馆。

reading.title: Writing It Down
reading.passage: Lin kept no record of what she spent during her first term. By December she had borrowed money from a roommate twice and could not explain where it had gone. In January she began writing every purchase in a small notebook: bus fares, snacks, a concert ticket, even a bottle of water. She did not try to spend less at first. She only wanted to see the numbers. After three weeks she noticed that small buys between classes came to more than her monthly phone bill. She started carrying a bottle from home and buying fruit at the market instead of at the campus shop. Nothing felt like a sacrifice, she says, because she had not given anything up. By the end of the term she had saved enough to buy a second-hand bicycle. Her roommate now keeps the same notebook.

questions.q: What did Lin do at first to change her spending?
options: She simply wrote down every purchase.
questions.explain: She did not try to spend less at first. She only wanted to see the numbers.（先只记录，不刻意省）

questions.q: What did she discover after three weeks?
options: Her phone bill was too high.
Small purchases added up to a large amount.
questions.explain: small buys between classes came to more than her monthly phone bill.

questions.q: Why did the changes not feel like a sacrifice?
options: She had more money than before.
She did not feel she had given anything up.
Her parents paid for the bicycle.
questions.explain: because she had not given anything up（因为她并不觉得自己放弃了什么）。

reading.title: Walking Football
reading.passage: Walking football looks like ordinary football with one important difference: players are not allowed to run. If you run, the other team gets a free kick. The game was designed for people over fifty who want to keep moving without hurting their knees. Our town club started with six members two years ago; it now has more than forty, including several who had not played any sport since school. Matches are short, and everyone plays the same amount of time. Because speed no longer decides the result, passing and positioning matter more. Members say the best part is not the score but the half hour of talk afterwards. One of them, a retired bus driver, puts it simply: at our age, you win by turning up.

questions.q: What is the main rule of walking football?
questions.explain: players are not allowed to run（不许跑）。

questions.q: For whom was the game designed?
questions.explain: designed for people over fifty who want to keep moving without hurting their knees.

questions.q: What does the retired bus driver mean by "you win by turning up"?
options: Taking part matters more than the result.
questions.explain: 与前文 the best part is not the score 呼应：在这个年纪，能来参与本身就是胜利。

reading.title: A Easier Return
reading.passage: Returning goods bought online used to be a slow business at our local shop. Customers had to print a form, find a box and take the parcel to a different counter. Last year the shop changed the whole process. Now a customer shows the order code on a phone, an assistant scans it, and the refund is sent within two days. No printing is needed, and the shop supplies the box. Staff were trained to handle returns at the same desk where they sell goods, so nobody is sent to another queue. The manager expected complaints about the extra work. Instead, returns rose by a fifth, but so did sales. Her explanation is short: people buy more readily when they know that changing their mind is easy. Other shops in the street have since copied the idea.

questions.q: What did customers have to do before last year?
options: Bring the seller to the shop
Print a form and go to a different counter
questions.explain: had to print a form, find a box and take the parcel to a different counter.

questions.q: What happened after the process changed?
options: The shop closed the return service.
questions.explain: returns rose by a fifth, but so did sales（退货量和销售额都涨了）。

questions.q: What is the manager's explanation?
options: Easy returns make people more willing to buy.
questions.explain: people buy more readily when they know that changing their mind is easy.

reading.title: A Message Before the Rain
reading.passage: The city's weather service began sending short text messages to farmers two years ago. Before that, most growers relied on the radio or simply looked at the sky. Now, if heavy rain is expected within six hours, a message reaches every registered phone in the district. It says when the rain will start, how long it may last and what to do about young plants. The service is free, and signing up takes one minute at the village office. In the first year, fewer than half the farmers joined. Many did not trust a message more than their own experience. That changed after one storm in July, when those who received the warning covered their seedlings and lost almost nothing. This spring, nine out of ten growers in the district are on the list. The service now plans to add wind and frost warnings as well.

questions.q: How did most growers get weather information before?
options: From the radio or by looking at the sky
questions.explain: most growers relied on the radio or simply looked at the sky.

questions.q: Why did many farmers not join at first?
options: They trusted their own experience more.
questions.explain: Many did not trust a message more than their own experience.

questions.q: What made most farmers change their minds?
options: A July storm in which warned farmers lost almost nothing
questions.explain: that changed after one storm in July, when those who received the warning covered their seedlings and lost almost nothing.

reading.title: The Feed That Knows You
reading.passage: Recommendation systems are usually defended on the grounds of convenience: they spare us the labour of choosing. What is less often discussed is how quietly they narrow the choosing itself. A platform that learns which articles you finish will, quite rationally, offer more of the same, because a satisfied reader is a returning one. Over months, the range of what appears on the screen can contract without the reader ever being told that anything was removed. Researchers call this a filter bubble, though the metaphor is mildly misleading — nothing has been sealed, and a determined reader can still search elsewhere. The more accurate complaint is about defaults. Most people do not search elsewhere; they take what is placed in front of them. Regulators have accordingly begun to ask not whether platforms censor, but whether the option to see a different ordering is visible at all. That question is harder to answer, and considerably more useful.

questions.q: How are recommendation systems usually defended?
options: They save users the effort of choosing.
They protect users from harmful content.
They increase the number of articles written.
questions.explain: on the grounds of convenience: they spare us the labour of choosing（以便利为由：省去选择的力气）。

questions.q: What does the author say about the term "filter bubble"?
options: It slightly misleads, because nothing is actually sealed.
It applies only to search engines.
questions.explain: the metaphor is mildly misleading — nothing has been sealed（这个比喻有点误导，因为并没有被封起来）。

questions.q: What is the author's main point about the real problem?
options: The issue is the default ordering that most people accept.
Readers are too lazy to read long articles.
Regulators have already solved the problem.
questions.explain: The more accurate complaint is about defaults… they take what is placed in front of them（问题在于多数人接受的默认排序）。

questions.q: What is the author's attitude towards the regulators' new question?
questions.explain: 末句 That question is harder to answer, and considerably more useful（更难、也更有用）——明显是肯定的。

reading.title: The Office After the Office
reading.passage: When a large technology firm moved most of its staff to remote work, managers expected the main difficulty to be technical. It was not. Within a year the complaint that surfaced most often was subtler: junior employees no longer knew how the work was actually decided. In a shared room, a newcomer learns by overhearing — who asks which question, when a silence means disagreement, how a compromise is reached. Video calls transmit the conclusion of such exchanges but rarely the exchange itself. Senior staff, meanwhile, reported fewer interruptions and higher satisfaction, which made the discrepancy easy to miss. The firm's response was not to call everyone back. It created short, documented decision reviews in which the reasoning behind a choice is written down and opened to questions. Whether this substitutes for presence remains uncertain. What the episode suggests is that the value of an office lay less in its desks than in the accidental education it provided.

questions.q: What problem did junior employees report?
options: They could not see how decisions were actually made.
questions.explain: junior employees no longer knew how the work was actually decided.

questions.q: Why was the problem easy to overlook?
options: Senior staff were more satisfied and less interrupted.
questions.explain: Senior staff… reported fewer interruptions and higher satisfaction, which made the discrepancy easy to miss.

questions.q: What does "accidental education" refer to?
options: Learning by overhearing how experienced colleagues work
questions.explain: a newcomer learns by overhearing（新人靠旁听学到东西）——即无意中获得的经验。

questions.q: What is the author's tone towards the firm's solution?
questions.explain: Whether this substitutes for presence remains uncertain（是否替代得了在场，仍不确定）——措辞审慎。

reading.title: The Last Speakers
reading.passage: A language is often declared dead on the strength of a number: the count of people who still speak it at home. That measure is convenient, and it is misleading. In several communities studied recently, fluent speakers in their seventies use the language mainly with one another, while their grandchildren understand it but answer in the dominant tongue. Whether the language survives depends less on this generation's vocabulary than on whether anyone has a reason to use it tomorrow. Recording the elders is therefore necessary but not sufficient; an archive preserves a voice, not a conversation. The projects that appear to work are modest and unromantic. They pay for a weekly market stall where the language is the normal way to bargain, or for a radio hour of local news. Such efforts rarely produce a dictionary. They produce something harder to count and more decisive: a setting in which speaking the language is simply what one does.

questions.q: Why does the author call the speaker count misleading?
options: It ignores whether the language has a context in which it is used.
questions.explain: depends less on this generation's vocabulary than on whether anyone has a reason to use it tomorrow（关键是有没有使用场合）。

questions.q: What does "an archive preserves a voice, not a conversation" mean?
options: Recording alone does not keep a language in use.
Conversations are too long to record.
questions.explain: 录音保存的是声音，而不是活生生的交谈——单靠存档无法让语言继续被使用。

questions.q: What do the successful projects have in common?
options: They create everyday situations where the language is used naturally.
questions.explain: a setting in which speaking the language is simply what one does（营造自然语言使用场景）。

questions.q: Which word best describes the author's view of the projects?
questions.explain: modest and unromantic、rarely produce a dictionary 但 more decisive——务实地肯定其效果。

reading.title: Cooler Streets
reading.passage: Cities are routinely several degrees warmer than the countryside around them, a difference produced by dark surfaces, sparse vegetation and the heat released by buildings. The effect is not evenly distributed. Mapping studies in several large cities show that the hottest districts are frequently those with the fewest trees, and that these are often the same districts with the oldest housing and the lowest incomes. This correlation has turned a technical question about materials into a question about fairness. Planting trees sounds like a simple remedy, yet it is slow: a sapling provides little shade for a decade, and in dry regions it needs water that may itself be scarce. Some planners therefore favour lighter pavements and reflective roofs, which cool a street immediately. Others warn that such measures, precisely because they are quick, can be used to postpone the slower investment. The sensible reading is not that one approach wins, but that the timing of benefit matters as much as its size.

questions.q: What produces the temperature difference between city and countryside?
options: Dark surfaces, little vegetation and heat from buildings
Fewer people living in rural areas
questions.explain: produced by dark surfaces, sparse vegetation and the heat released by buildings.

questions.q: Why has the issue become a question about fairness?
options: The hottest districts often have older housing and lower incomes.
Reflective roofs are only available to the rich.
questions.explain: the hottest districts… are often the same districts with the oldest housing and the lowest incomes.

questions.q: What disadvantage of planting trees is mentioned?
options: Trees increase the need for air conditioning.
A young tree gives little shade for years and needs water.
questions.explain: a sapling provides little shade for a decade, and in dry regions it needs water.

questions.q: What does the last sentence imply?
options: Quick fixes should always be preferred.
Only large benefits are worth pursuing.
When a benefit arrives is as important as how large it is.
questions.explain: the timing of benefit matters as much as its size（见效时间与效果大小同样重要）。

reading.title: Who Should Hold the Objects
reading.passage: Debates about returning cultural objects are usually conducted as arguments about ownership, and that framing makes them hard to settle. Legal title, where it exists, is often clear; what is contested is whether a clear title is the same as a just one. Museums point to conservation: they have the climate control, the staff and the records that many objects would lack elsewhere. Institutions in countries of origin reply that preservation is not the only value at stake, and that an object kept behind glass far from the community that made it preserves material while severing meaning. Both claims are serious. What has changed is not the law but the willingness of museums to admit that their founding collections were assembled under conditions no longer defended. Several have begun long-term loans, shared catalogues and joint research rather than outright transfer. Critics call this a half-measure. It may also be the only arrangement durable enough to survive a change of government.

questions.q: Why are these debates hard to settle according to the author?
options: The law is unclear in every case.
No records of the objects survive.
They are framed as ownership, while the real dispute is about justice.
questions.explain: framed as arguments about ownership… whether a clear title is the same as a just one（争的是正当性而非名义所有权）。

questions.q: What is the museums' main argument?
options: They can preserve the objects better.
The objects have no meaning now.
questions.explain: Museums point to conservation: they have the climate control, the staff and the records.

questions.q: What does "severing meaning" mean?
options: Separating an object from the culture that gives it significance
questions.explain: preserves material while severing meaning：保住了实物，却切断了它与原社群的意义联系。

questions.q: What is the author's view of long-term loans and joint research?
options: They are worse than doing nothing.
They are a practical compromise that may last.
questions.explain: 末句：可能是唯一「足够持久、能熬过政府更迭」的安排——视其为务实且耐久的折中。

reading.title: The Price of a Tap
reading.passage: Water is almost everywhere treated differently from other goods, and for good reason: a household cannot reasonably choose to do without it. Yet the way it is priced often assumes that demand behaves as it would for anything else. In many cities the first units consumed are charged at a low rate intended to cover basic needs, while heavy use is charged more steeply. The design is defensible, but its effects are uneven. A large family on a modest income may reach the expensive band simply by having more children, whereas a single person in a spacious flat never does. Metering, meanwhile, is frequently least reliable in the oldest districts, exactly where consumption is hardest to estimate. Economists tend to discuss such problems as matters of efficiency. Residents describe them in a different vocabulary — as fairness. Neither account is wrong; they simply measure different things, and a tariff has to answer to both.

questions.q: Why is water treated differently from other goods?
options: Households cannot reasonably go without it.
It is owned by the state everywhere.
questions.explain: a household cannot reasonably choose to do without it.

questions.q: What problem does the pricing design create?
options: A large low-income family may reach the expensive band just by having more children.
It discourages all use of water.
Single people pay the highest rate.
questions.explain: A large family on a modest income may reach the expensive band simply by having more children.

questions.q: What does the last sentence suggest about a tariff?
options: Efficiency is the only valid measure.
It must satisfy both efficiency and fairness.
questions.explain: Neither account is wrong… a tariff has to answer to both（两种标准都要顾及）。

questions.q: What is the author's tone?
questions.explain: 既指出设计 defensible（可辩护）又指出 effects are uneven（效果不均），末句承认两种视角都不错——克制且平衡。

reading.title: The Line Already Filled In
reading.passage: Few policy tools are as quiet as a pre-ticked box. When a form arrives with a choice already made, most people leave it alone — not because they have weighed the matter and agreed, but because changing a default requires an extra step and a moment's attention. Studies of organ-donation registers and retirement savings show the same pattern across countries: where enrolment is automatic, participation is high; where a box must be ticked, it falls sharply, even though the underlying decision is identical. Defenders call this helpful nudging, since most people say they intend to enrol anyway. Critics reply that an intention never acted upon is not obviously the same as consent, and that the ease of opting out matters less than whether anyone noticed the option existed. The empirical finding is not really in dispute. What remains contested is whether a result that people would have chosen counts as a choice they made.

questions.q: Why do most people leave a pre-ticked box unchanged?
options: They have carefully considered and agreed.
Changing it takes an extra step and attention.
They do not understand the form.
questions.explain: changing a default requires an extra step and a moment's attention.

questions.q: What do the studies show across countries?
options: Automatic enrolment leads to much higher participation.
questions.explain: where enrolment is automatic, participation is high; where a box must be ticked, it falls sharply.

questions.q: What do critics question?
options: Whether an unacted-upon intention counts as consent
questions.explain: an intention never acted upon is not obviously the same as consent.

questions.q: What is the central issue according to the last sentence?
options: How to design a clearer form
Whether an outcome people would have chosen is a choice they actually made
questions.explain: whether a result that people would have chosen counts as a choice they made（「本会选的结果」是否等于「做出的选择」）。

reading.title: The Fifth Day
reading.passage: Trials of a four-day week tend to be reported in one of two ways: either as proof that shorter hours cost nothing, or as evidence that they cannot last. Both readings simplify what the trials actually measure. Most involve firms that volunteered, which is to say firms already confident that their work could be reorganised; the least suitable cases never entered the sample. Output is usually held constant by removing meetings rather than by speeding people up, a gain that may be available only once. Employees, unsurprisingly, report better sleep and less intention to leave — outcomes that matter, but that are not the same as productivity. None of this makes the trials worthless. It does mean that the honest conclusion is narrower than the headlines: for some kinds of work, under some conditions, a shorter week can be introduced without an immediate loss. Whether it generalises is a question about organisations, not about the calendar.

questions.q: Why does the author say both common readings are too simple?
options: Participating firms were volunteers likely suited to shorter hours.
The trials measured neither productivity nor attendance.
The trials lasted only one week.
questions.explain: Most involve firms that volunteered… the least suitable cases never entered the sample（样本本身有选择性）。

questions.q: How is output usually kept constant in the trials?
questions.explain: by removing meetings rather than by speeding people up.

questions.q: What does the author say about better sleep and lower turnover?
options: They are valuable but not the same as productivity.
They prove the four-day week always works.
questions.explain: outcomes that matter, but that are not the same as productivity.

questions.q: What is the main conclusion of the passage?
options: A four-day week should be adopted everywhere.
The trials were badly designed and prove nothing.
Governments should legislate a shorter week.
The results are real but limited to certain kinds of work and conditions.
questions.explain: for some kinds of work, under some conditions… without an immediate loss（结论有条件、范围更窄）。

reading.title: The Quiet Study Corner
reading.passage: Our school library recently opened a small 'quiet corner' on the second floor. Unlike the busy reading halls, this area has soft chairs, warm lights, and no talking allowed. At first, few students went there. But after a poster described it as 'a place to slow down', more people started to use it between classes. Now it is often full in the afternoon. Librarians say students tell them they can focus better in the calm space, and some even finish homework faster than at home.

questions.q: Why was the quiet corner first unpopular?
options: It was too far from the entrance.
Few students knew about it at first.
It was only open at night.
questions.explain: 第一段说 At first, few students went there，随后靠海报宣传才更多人使用，说明起初知道的人少。

questions.q: What can we learn about the quiet corner?
options: Talking is allowed in small groups.
It helps some students focus better.
It is always empty in the afternoon.
questions.explain: 末句提到学生在安静空间更能集中注意力，有些人比在家完成作业更快。

questions.q: What is the writer's attitude toward the quiet corner?
questions.explain: 作者用 positive 词汇（focus better, finish faster）描述，态度是支持的。

reading.title: Walking to Work
reading.passage: A small study followed 200 office workers who changed from driving to walking or cycling to work. After three months, most reported better moods and slept more easily at night. The researchers said the effect was not only from exercise; the time outdoors and the sense of starting the day actively also helped. However, those with very long distances found it hard to keep the habit in bad weather. The team suggested beginning with just two days a week.

questions.q: What did most workers experience after three months?
options: They felt happier and slept better.
questions.explain: 第二段说 most reported better moods and slept more easily，即情绪更好、睡眠更佳。

questions.q: Besides exercise, what else helped according to the study?
options: Time outdoors and an active start.
questions.explain: 研究者指出户外时间与积极开启一天的感觉也起作用。

questions.q: What did the team suggest for beginners?
options: Start with two days a week.
questions.explain: 末句团队建议从每周两天开始。

reading.title: Smartphone Reminders
reading.passage: Many people use phone reminders to remember meetings, bills, and even to drink water. A survey found that while reminders reduce forgetfulness, they may also make us rely on the phone too much. Some users said they stopped remembering things on their own. Experts suggest using reminders for important tasks but still writing key dates on paper. They believe the act of writing helps the brain keep information.

questions.q: What is one problem with phone reminders mentioned?
options: They may make people depend on the phone.
questions.explain: 文中说 reminders 可能让人过度依赖手机，不再自己记忆。

questions.q: What do experts recommend?
options: Use reminders but also write key dates.
questions.explain: 专家建议对重要事项用提醒，但仍把关键日期写在纸上。

questions.q: Why might writing on paper help?
options: The act of writing helps the brain remember.
questions.explain: 专家认为书写动作有助于大脑保留信息。

reading.title: Free Weekend Museums
reading.passage: The city decided to open its three main museums for free on the first Sunday of every month. Officials hoped more families would visit and learn together. In the first three months, visits rose by 40%. Some visitors said they had never been because of the cost. Museum workers noticed that children asked more questions and seemed more curious. The program will continue next year if the budget allows.

questions.q: What was the goal of the free Sunday plan?
options: To let more families visit and learn.
questions.explain: 官员希望更多家庭能一起参观学习。

questions.q: What happened in the first three months?
questions.explain: 前三个月参观量上升了 40%。

questions.q: Will the program continue?
questions.explain: 文中说若预算允许，明年将继续。

reading.title: Breakfast Matters
reading.passage: Skipping breakfast is common among busy students, but a school health report warns against it. The report shows that students who eat a morning meal score higher on memory tests and feel less tired by noon. Teachers also notice better behavior in class. The report does not ask for a big meal; even a piece of fruit and a glass of milk can help. It suggests keeping easy food at home for rushed mornings.

questions.q: What does the health report say about breakfast?
options: It should be a big meal.
It helps memory and reduces tiredness.
questions.explain: 报告显示吃早餐者在记忆测试中得分更高、中午更不易疲劳。

questions.q: What do teachers observe?
questions.explain: 老师注意到课堂行为更好。

questions.q: What does the report suggest for busy mornings?
questions.explain: 建议在家备好简便食物应对匆忙的早晨。

reading.title: The Community Run
reading.passage: Every spring, our town holds a 5-kilometer run to raise money for the children's hospital. Last year, over 800 people joined, including whole families and a few dogs. Volunteers gave out water and cheered at every corner. A local baker donated bread for the finish line. The event collected enough to buy new toys and books. Organizers say the real success is not the money but the happy faces.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the community run?
options: To raise money for a children's hospital.
questions.explain: 小镇举办 5 公里跑为儿童医院筹款。

questions.q: Who took part in the event?
questions.explain: 800 多人参加，包括全家、几只狗和志愿者。

questions.q: What does the organizer value most?
questions.explain: 组织者说真正的成功不是钱，而是人们快乐的笑脸。

reading.title: The 15-Minute City
reading.passage: The '15-minute city' is an urban plan in which daily needs—work, shops, schools, parks—are reachable within a short walk or bike ride from home. Supporters argue it cuts traffic and pollution while improving community life. Critics worry it may raise housing prices in well-served areas and overlook people who must travel for specialized jobs. Several European cities have tested the idea with mixed results. Planners stress that success depends less on the slogan and more on affordable housing and good public transport.

questions.q: What is the core idea of a '15-minute city'?
options: Daily needs are close to home.
questions.explain: 核心理念是工作、购物、学校等日常需求步行或骑车短时可及。

questions.q: What is a concern raised by critics?
options: It may raise housing prices in served areas.
It forces people to quit jobs.
questions.explain: 批评者担心配套完善区域房价上涨，并忽视需通勤者。

questions.q: According to planners, what determines success?
questions.explain: 规划者强调成败更取决于可负担住房与优质公交，而非口号。

questions.q: What word best describes the test results so far?
questions.explain: 文中用 mixed results 描述试点结果，即喜忧参半。

reading.title: The Science of Rest
reading.passage: We often think of rest as simply not working, yet research shows that passive scrolling on a phone is not true rest for the brain. Active rest—such as a walk, a short nap, or focused breathing—lowers stress hormones more effectively. A 2023 study found that workers who took a 20-minute walk at midday reported steadier attention in the afternoon than those who browsed social media. The authors caution that rest is not a reward for finishing work but a condition for doing it well.

questions.q: What does the passage say about phone scrolling?
options: It is the best form of rest.
It is not true rest for the brain.
questions.explain: 研究指出被动刷手机并非大脑真正的休息。

questions.q: Which activity lowered stress more in the study?
questions.explain: 研究发现午间步行 20 分钟者下午注意力更稳。

questions.q: How do the authors view rest?
questions.explain: 作者提醒休息不是完成工作后的奖赏，而是做好工作的前提。

reading.title: Remote Work and Cities
reading.passage: The shift to remote work has changed more than schedules; it has reshaped city economies. Downtown shops that once served office workers now struggle, while neighborhoods see more foot traffic and new cafes. Some economists predict a slow but lasting move toward 'hub-and-spoke' work, where employees go to a nearby office a few days a week. Others warn that tax bases built on central business districts may need rethinking. The full effect remains uncertain, but the map of daily life has clearly shifted.

questions.q: What has remote work changed according to the passage?
questions.explain: 远程办公重塑了城市经济与日常生活地图。

questions.q: What is 'hub-and-spoke' work?
options: Going to a nearby office a few days a week.
questions.explain: 文中解释为员工每周数天去就近办公室的模式。

questions.q: What concern do some economists raise?
options: Tax bases relying on city centers may need rethinking.
questions.explain: 一些经济学家警告依赖中央商务区的税基可能需要重新考量。

reading.title: AI and Routine Jobs
reading.passage: As AI tools improve, routine office tasks such as drafting emails and summarizing reports are increasingly automated. This worries some workers, yet many managers report that the technology frees them to focus on judgment and creativity. A survey of 1,000 employees found that those who used AI assistants spent less time on repetitive work and more on problem-solving. The report concludes that the skill of working with AI, not competing against it, will define the next decade of office work.

questions.q: What tasks are increasingly automated?
options: Routine tasks like emails and summaries.
questions.explain: 起草邮件、总结报告等常规办公任务日益被自动化。

questions.q: What did the survey of 1,000 employees find?
questions.explain: 使用 AI 助手者重复性工作减少、解决问题时间增多。

questions.q: What does the report say will define the next decade?
options: The skill of working with AI.
questions.explain: 与 AI 协作的能力而非与之竞争，将定义未来十年。

reading.title: Who Owns a Recipe?
reading.passage: When a popular restaurant published its grandmother's recipe online, a debate followed: can a family dish be 'owned'? Food historians note that nearly all recipes are built on earlier ones, borrowed and changed across generations. Copyright law generally protects written expression, not the dish itself, so others may cook and even sell a similar version. Still, many chefs now credit their sources openly, arguing that respect, not law, is what keeps culinary tradition alive.

questions.q: What debate did the recipe post cause?
options: Whether a family dish can be owned.
questions.explain: 争议在于一道家传菜能否被'拥有'。

questions.q: What does copyright law usually protect?
questions.explain: 版权一般保护书面表达，而非菜肴本身。

questions.q: How do many chefs show respect today?
questions.explain: 许多厨师公开注明来源以示尊重。

reading.title: The Life of a Smartphone
reading.passage: A smartphone's environmental cost begins long before purchase: mining rare metals, building components, and shipping all consume energy and water. Yet the biggest impact often comes from how long we keep the device. Studies show that extending a phone's life by two years can cut its total carbon footprint by nearly a third. Repair-friendly design and second-hand markets help, but consumers' habit of upgrading every year remains the hardest barrier to change.

questions.q: When does a smartphone's environmental cost begin?
options: Long before purchase, during mining and making.
questions.explain: 环境成本在购前开采金属、制造与运输阶段就产生了。

questions.q: What reduces the carbon footprint most, per the studies?
options: Keeping the phone two years longer.
questions.explain: 研究称延长使用两年可削减近三分之一碳足迹。

questions.q: What is called the hardest barrier?
questions.explain: 消费者每年换新的习惯被视为最难改变的障碍。

writing.title: On Balancing Study and Club Activities
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on the topic Balancing Study and Club Activities. You should explain why it matters and how college students can strike a balance.
writing.promptZh: 论述大学生为何及如何在学习与社团活动之间取得平衡。
outline: 第一段：指出大学生活中学习与社团活动常常难以兼顾的现象
第二段：说明平衡的重要性并给出具体做法（制定计划、分清主次）
第三段：总结——平衡两者才能全面发展
writing.model: Nowadays, many college students find it hard to balance study and club activities. Some devote so much time to clubs that their grades suffer, while others study all day and miss chances to develop social skills. In my opinion, a good balance is essential. First, we should make a weekly schedule and stick to it, setting aside time for both lectures and club meetings. Second, learning to say no to unimportant activities helps us focus on what really matters. In short, study lays the foundation for our future, while clubs make college life colorful. Only by balancing the two can we grow into well-rounded people.

expressions.en: strike a balance between A and B

writing.title: How to Take Notes Effectively
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on the topic How to Take Notes Effectively. You should suggest at least two methods and explain why they work.
writing.promptZh: 谈谈如何有效地记课堂笔记，给出至少两种方法并说明理由。
outline: 第一段：指出记笔记是高效学习的重要手段
第二段：提出具体方法（抓重点、用自己的话、课后复习）
第三段：总结——好笔记贵在坚持与整理
writing.model: Taking notes is one of the most useful study habits, yet many students simply copy whatever the teacher writes on the blackboard. This is far from effective. To begin with, we should listen carefully and write down key points instead of every word, because our brain stays active when we select information. Besides, putting ideas into our own words makes them easier to understand and remember. Last but not least, reviewing notes right after class helps move knowledge into long-term memory. In conclusion, effective note-taking is not about writing more but about thinking more. With regular practice, it will surely improve our study efficiency.

writing.title: The Importance of Communicating with Parents
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on the importance of communicating with parents. You should explain why many students neglect it and how to improve family communication.
writing.promptZh: 论述与父母沟通的重要性，分析学生忽视沟通的原因并提出改进建议。
outline: 第一段：现象——大学生离家后与父母联系变少
第二段：说明沟通的意义（父母关心我们、减少误解）及做法（定期打电话、分享生活）
第三段：总结——亲情需要用心维系
writing.model: After entering college, many students call their parents only when they need money. They complain that their parents do not understand them, yet they seldom share their real lives at home. In fact, communication is the bridge between hearts. Our parents worry about us and long to know how we are doing, and a weekly phone call can easily put their minds at rest. Moreover, honest talks help clear up misunderstandings before they turn into arguments. Family love does not keep itself alive; it needs to be tended. So let us pick up the phone tonight and tell Mom and Dad about our day.

writing.title: Say No to Phone Addiction
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on the topic of phone addiction among college students. You should describe the problem, state its harm, and suggest ways to use phones wisely.
writing.promptZh: 描述大学生手机成瘾问题及其危害，并提出合理使用手机的建议。
outline: 第一段：现象——低头族遍布校园，学生沉迷手机
第二段：危害（影响视力与睡眠、减少面对面交流、耽误学习）
第三段：建议（限定使用时间、培养线下爱好）并总结
writing.model: Walk across any campus today, and you will see heads bowed over glowing screens. Many students check their phones hundreds of times a day, unable to focus even on a single meal. Such addiction does great harm. It damages our eyesight, steals our sleep and, worse still, weakens real-life relationships, since face-to-face talks are replaced by cold messages. To break free, we can set a daily time limit for social media apps and keep phones away from the bedside at night. Developing offline hobbies like reading or jogging also helps. A phone should be a useful tool, not a master that controls our lives.

expressions.en: a useful tool rather than a master
expressions.zh: 是有用的工具而非主宰

writing.title: Benefits of Regular Exercise
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on the benefits of regular exercise. You should give at least two benefits and encourage students to work out.
writing.promptZh: 论述经常锻炼的益处，至少给出两点，并鼓励大家坚持运动。
outline: 第一段：现象——很多学生久坐不动，忽视锻炼
第二段：益处（增强体质、缓解压力、提高学习效率）
第三段：号召——从小事做起，坚持锻炼
writing.model: With heavy schoolwork and attractive screens, many college students sit for hours without moving. However, a strong body is the basis of everything we dream of. Regular exercise brings at least two clear benefits. For one thing, it builds up our muscles and strengthens our immune system, keeping illness at a distance. For another, physical activity releases stress; after a run or a game of basketball, we usually feel relaxed and cheerful, which in turn improves our study efficiency. Exercise does not have to be painful. Taking the stairs, cycling to class or jogging half an hour a day all count. Let us move today for a healthier tomorrow.

writing.title: My View on Part-time Jobs
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on whether college students should take part-time jobs. You should discuss both the advantages and the risks, and give your opinion.
writing.promptZh: 讨论大学生做兼职的利与弊，并表明自己的看法。
outline: 第一段：引出话题——兼职在大学生中很流行
第二段：分析利（赚钱、积累经验）与弊（占用学习时间、可能受骗）
第三段：表明观点——量力而行，学习优先
writing.model: Part-time jobs have become increasingly popular on campus. Some students work as tutors or waiters in their spare time, while others prefer to focus entirely on study. In my view, a part-time job is a double-edged sword. On the one hand, it helps us earn pocket money, understand the value of labor and gain social experience that textbooks cannot offer. On the other hand, working too many hours may eat into our study time, and inexperienced students can even fall victim to cheating employers. Therefore, we should choose jobs carefully and always put study first. Only then can part-time work truly benefit our growth.

expressions.en: on the one hand ... on the other hand

writing.title: Building a Green Campus
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on how to build a green campus. You should point out some wasteful behaviors and suggest what students can do.
writing.promptZh: 指出校园中的浪费现象，并从学生角度提出建设绿色校园的建议。
outline: 第一段：现象——校园里存在长明灯、长流水、食物浪费等问题
第二段：原因与建议（节约水电、光盘行动、垃圾分类）
第三段：总结——绿色校园靠每个人的举手之劳
writing.model: Lights burning in empty classrooms, taps left running and untouched food thrown away — such scenes are still common on our campus. Waste not only costs money but also harms the environment we depend on. To build a green campus, every student can take small actions. First, turn off lights and air conditioners when leaving a room, and use both sides of paper. Second, order only what we can finish at the canteen and say no to disposable chopsticks. Third, sort rubbish so that waste can be recycled. Green habits cost little but mean much. If each of us does our bit, our campus will become cleaner and greener.

writing.title: Why We Should Read More Books
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on why college students should read more books. You should explain the value of reading and give a suggestion on how to develop the habit.
writing.promptZh: 论述大学生多读书的价值，并就如何养成阅读习惯给出建议。
outline: 第一段：现象——短视频流行，读书的人越来越少
第二段：读书的价值（开阔视野、启迪思想、提升表达）
第三段：建议——每天固定时间读书，让阅读成为习惯
writing.model: In an age of short videos, fewer and fewer students open a book. Yet reading remains one of the cheapest ways to enrich ourselves. Books open a window onto worlds we may never visit and let us talk with the wisest minds in history. Through reading, we broaden our horizons, sharpen our thinking and improve our writing. To develop this good habit, we can set aside half an hour every evening, leave our phones in another room and choose books that truly interest us. As the old saying goes, books are the ladder of human progress. The more we read, the further we can see.

writing.title: What Travel Brings Us
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on the topic What Travel Brings Us. You should state the benefits of traveling and share your own attitude toward it.
writing.promptZh: 谈谈旅行带来的好处，并表达自己对旅行的态度。
outline: 第一段：引出话题——旅行成为大学生假期热门选择
第二段：益处（欣赏风景、体验文化、锻炼独立与交际能力）
第三段：态度——旅行不必奢侈，重要的是走出去看世界
writing.model: Traveling has become a favorite way for college students to spend their holidays. Its benefits are obvious. First, traveling allows us to enjoy beautiful scenery and experience different customs, which enriches our knowledge beyond textbooks. Second, on the road we have to buy tickets, find hotels and talk with strangers, so our independence and social skills are greatly improved. Moreover, travel relieves pressure and refreshes the mind. Of course, travel need not be expensive; even a trip to a nearby town can surprise us. As a proverb says, he who does not travel reads only one page of the book of life. Let us go out and read more pages.

expressions.en: read only one page of the book of life
expressions.zh: 只读了人生之书的一页

writing.title: Learn to Manage Our Time
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on the importance of time management for college students. You should explain why time is easily wasted and how to manage it well.
writing.promptZh: 论述大学生时间管理的重要性，分析时间浪费的原因并提出管理办法。
outline: 第一段：现象——许多学生抱怨时间不够用却仍在刷手机
第二段：原因（缺乏计划、拖延）与办法（列清单、分清轻重缓急、立即行动）
第三段：总结——做时间的主人
writing.model: Many students complain that there is never enough time, yet hours slip away as they scroll through short videos. Time is fair to everyone: it never stops or waits. The real problem lies in poor management. Without a plan, we tend to deal with whatever comes first and put off important tasks. To manage time well, we should list our tasks every morning and rank them by importance. Then we start with the most difficult one while our energy is high. Small pockets of time, such as the queue at the canteen, can be used for memorizing words. Whoever controls the minutes controls the day.

writing.title: A Letter Inviting a Friend to a Lecture
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a letter of about 80-100 words to your friend Lily, inviting her to attend a lecture on English learning given by Professor Wang this Friday evening. Include the time, place and your reasons for the invitation.
writing.promptZh: 给朋友Lily写一封邀请信，邀请她本周五晚听王教授的英语学习讲座，写明时间地点与邀请理由。
outline: 第一段：问候并说明写信目的——邀请听讲座
第二段：介绍讲座信息（时间、地点、内容）及邀请理由
第三段：希望对方接受邀请并盼回复
writing.model:
Dear Lily,
How is everything going? I am writing to invite you to a lecture on English learning given by Professor Wang this Friday evening at 7:00 in the university library hall. Professor Wang is famous for his practical methods, and he will share useful tips on vocabulary building and listening practice. Since you have been preparing for the CET-4 exam, I believe this lecture will be of great help to you. Seats are limited, so if you are interested, please let me know by Wednesday and I will get tickets for both of us. Looking forward to your reply.
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

expressions.en: I am writing to invite you to...
expressions.zh: 我写信是想邀请你参加……

expressions.en: be of great help to sb.

writing.title: An Email Asking About an English Course
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write an email of about 80-100 words to the Training Center, asking about its evening English course. Your email should cover the schedule, class size, fees and how to sign up.
writing.promptZh: 给培训中心写一封邮件，咨询其英语晚课的时间安排、班级人数、费用及报名方式。
outline: 第一段：说明写信目的——咨询英语课程
第二段：列出具体问题（上课时间、人数、学费、报名流程）
第三段：表示感谢并盼回复
writing.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I am a sophomore majoring in chemistry, and I am interested in the evening English course offered by your center. I am writing to ask for some detailed information. Could you please tell me when the classes begin and how many hours they last each week? I would also like to know the class size, since I prefer small classes with more chances to speak. Besides, what are the fees, and are there any discounts for students? Finally, how can I sign up, online or in person? Thank you for your time, and I look forward to your early reply.
Yours faithfully,
Li Ming

expressions.en: I am writing to ask for...
I look forward to your early reply.

writing.title: A Notice for an English Speech Contest
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a notice of about 80-100 words on behalf of the Students' Union, announcing an English speech contest to be held next month. The notice should include the theme, time, place, requirements and how to register.
writing.promptZh: 以学生会名义写一则英语演讲比赛通知，包含主题、时间地点、参赛要求与报名方式。
outline: 第一段：宣布比赛举办并点明主题
第二段：交代时间、地点、时长要求与报名截止时间、方式
第三段：欢迎参加并说明奖项设置
writing.model:
Notice
To enrich campus life and improve students' spoken English, the Students' Union will hold an English speech contest. The theme is "My Dream College Life". The contest will take place at 2:00 p.m. on Saturday, December 12, in Lecture Hall No. 1. Each speaker should give a three-minute speech in English, and slides are allowed. Any full-time student of our university is welcome to take part. Please sign up at the Students' Union office or by scanning the QR code on our official account before December 5. The top three winners will receive prizes and certificates. Come and show your talent!
Students' Union
November 20

writing.title: A Letter of Thanks to My Host Family
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a thank-you letter of about 80-100 words to the American host family you stayed with during a summer program. Express your gratitude, recall a happy moment and keep in touch.
writing.promptZh: 给暑期项目期间接待你的美国家庭写感谢信，表达感激、回忆美好瞬间并表示保持联系。
outline: 第一段：表达感谢并说明回国后一切安好
第二段：回忆具体的温暖细节（学做晚餐、周末远足）
第三段：邀请对方来中国做客并盼保持联系
writing.model:
Dear Mr. and Mrs. Smith,
I have been back in China for two weeks, and I often think of the days I spent with you. Words cannot fully express my gratitude for your warm hospitality. Thank you for teaching me how to make apple pie and for taking me hiking in the mountains on weekends. Those happy moments made my summer program unforgettable and greatly improved my spoken English. I still remember how patiently you corrected my pronunciation every evening. You are always welcome to visit China, and I would love to show you around my hometown. Please keep in touch, and give my best regards to your lovely daughter.
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

expressions.en: Words cannot fully express my gratitude.
expressions.zh: 言语无法充分表达我的感激。

writing.title: A Proposal on Saving Food
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a proposal of about 80-100 words calling on students to save food in the canteen. State the problem, its seriousness and at least two concrete suggestions.
writing.promptZh: 写一份倡议书，号召同学们在食堂节约粮食，指出问题与严重性并提出具体建议。
outline: 第一段：指出食堂食物浪费严重的问题
第二段：说明浪费的危害并提出具体建议（按需点餐、光盘行动、宣传提醒）
第三段：发出号召——从我做起，珍惜粮食
writing.model:
Dear fellow students,
Have you noticed the full buckets of leftovers in our canteen? It is reported that thousands of tons of grain are wasted on Chinese campuses every year, while many people in the world still suffer from hunger. This situation calls for our immediate action. Here are my suggestions. First, order only as much food as we can finish, and take smaller portions if necessary. Second, let us practice the "clean plate" habit and remind our classmates to do the same. Third, we can put up posters in the canteen to raise everyone's awareness. Saving food shows respect for farmers' hard work. Let us start with our own plates today!

writing.title: A Letter of Apology to My Teacher
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a letter of apology of about 80-100 words to Professor Chen, because you failed to hand in your paper on time due to illness. Explain the reason, apologize sincerely and promise a new date.
writing.promptZh: 给陈老师写一封道歉信，因病未按时交论文，说明原因、诚恳道歉并承诺补交时间。
outline: 第一段：直接致歉并说明迟交论文一事
第二段：解释原因（生病住院）并附证明
第三段：承诺补交时间，再次道歉
writing.model:
Dear Professor Chen,
I am writing to apologize for not handing in my term paper on time last Monday. Unfortunately, I caught a bad flu the night before the deadline and had to stay in the school hospital for three days, which made it impossible for me to finish the paper. Attached is the doctor's certificate. I have been working on it since I recovered, and I promise to submit the completed paper to your office before this Friday. I know deadlines are important, and I am truly sorry for any inconvenience caused. I will manage my schedule more carefully in the future.
Yours respectfully,
Li Ming

expressions.en: I am writing to apologize for...
make it impossible for sb. to do

writing.title: An Application Letter for a Summer Job
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write an application letter of about 80-100 words for a part-time English tutor position advertised by the Sunshine Education Center. Introduce yourself, state your strengths and express your wish for an interview.
writing.promptZh: 写一封求职信应聘阳光教育中心的英语家教兼职，自我介绍、说明优势并表达面试意愿。
outline: 第一段：说明信息来源与应聘职位
第二段：介绍专业、成绩与相关经验等自身优势
第三段：表达面试意愿并留下联系方式
writing.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing in response to your advertisement for a part-time English tutor. I am a junior majoring in English at the local university, and I passed the TEM-4 exam with a good grade last year. Over the past two years I have tutored three middle school students, whose English scores improved greatly, so I am confident in my teaching ability. Besides, I am patient, responsible and good at communicating with children. I can work at least four days a week during the summer vacation. I would appreciate an interview at your convenience, and my phone number is 138-0000-0000. Thank you for your consideration.
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

writing.title: Suggestions on Improving the School Library
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a letter of about 80-100 words to the head of the school library, pointing out some problems and giving at least two suggestions for improvement.
writing.promptZh: 给图书馆馆长写信，指出图书馆存在的问题并提出至少两条改进建议。
outline: 第一段：肯定图书馆作用并说明写信目的
第二段：指出问题（座位不足、旧书多）并提出建议（延长开放时间、更新藏书、线上预约）
第三段：希望建议被采纳并表示感谢
writing.model:
Dear Mr. Zhang,
As a frequent visitor to our school library, I am grateful for the quiet environment it provides. However, I would like to offer a few suggestions for its improvement. First, seats are always scarce before exams, so I suggest that the library open an online booking system, which would save students the trouble of queuing early in the morning. Second, many books on the shelves are outdated; it would be wonderful if new editions could be purchased every year. Finally, extending the opening hours on weekends would benefit those who need to study for long periods. I hope my suggestions will be helpful, and thank you for your hard work.
Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

expressions.en: I would like to offer a few suggestions.
save sb. the trouble of doing

writing.title: How to Get Along with Roommates
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on how to get along well with roommates. You should explain why conflicts happen and suggest ways to build a harmonious dormitory.
writing.promptZh: 分析宿舍矛盾产生的原因，并就如何与室友和谐相处提出建议。
outline: 第一段：现象——室友来自各地，生活习惯不同易生矛盾
第二段：建议（互相尊重、制定宿舍公约、及时沟通）
第三段：总结——和谐宿舍让大学生活更温暖
writing.model: Roommates come from different families and regions, so it is natural that they have different habits. One may stay up late while another gets up at dawn; small differences can easily grow into quarrels. To build a harmonious dormitory, mutual respect comes first. We should never laugh at others' habits or use their things without permission. Besides, it helps to work out simple dorm rules together, such as quiet hours after 11 p.m. Most importantly, when something bothers us, we should talk about it calmly instead of keeping silent and building up anger. A dormitory is more than a room to sleep in; with understanding, it becomes a second home.

writing.title: Online Shopping: Convenience and Problems
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on online shopping among college students. You should describe its convenience, point out possible problems and give your advice.
writing.promptZh: 谈大学生网购的便利与存在的问题，并给出你的建议。
outline: 第一段：现象——网购成为大学生主要购物方式
第二段：便利（省时、便宜、选择多）与问题（质量难保证、冲动消费）
第三段：建议——理性购物，选择正规平台
writing.model: With just a few clicks on the phone, everything from books to shoes can be delivered to the dormitory door. No wonder online shopping has become part of college life. Its advantages are clear: it saves time, offers lower prices and provides far more choices than local stores. However, problems cannot be ignored. Some products look much better in pictures than in reality, and the "double eleven" sales often tempt students into buying things they never need. In my opinion, we should shop on trusted platforms, read customers' reviews carefully and make a list before big sales. Enjoy the convenience, but stay rational.

writing.title: The Value of Volunteer Work
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on the value of volunteer work for college students. You should give examples and explain what volunteers can gain from it.
writing.promptZh: 论述大学生参加志愿服务的价值，举例说明志愿者能从中收获什么。
outline: 第一段：现象——越来越多大学生投身志愿服务
第二段：价值（帮助他人、锻炼能力、收获快乐与责任感），举例支教、敬老院服务
第三段：总结——赠人玫瑰，手有余香
writing.model: Nowadays, more and more college students spend their spare time as volunteers. They teach children in rural areas, guide visitors in museums and look after the elderly in nursing homes. Some people think volunteers only give without receiving anything, but I hold the opposite view. Volunteer work benefits the givers as much as the receivers. While helping others, we learn to communicate with strangers, organize activities and solve real problems — abilities that exams cannot measure. More importantly, the smiles of the people we help bring a deep sense of happiness and responsibility. As the saying goes, roses given, fragrance remains. Volunteering makes our youth truly meaningful.

writing.title: Healthy Eating on Campus
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on healthy eating habits among college students. Describe the unhealthy phenomena, explain the harm and give your suggestions.
writing.promptZh: 描述大学生中的不健康饮食现象及危害，并提出养成健康饮食习惯的建议。
outline: 第一段：现象——不吃早餐、常吃外卖、熬夜吃夜宵
第二段：危害（肠胃问题、肥胖、精力差）
第三段：建议（三餐规律、多吃蔬果、少点外卖）
writing.model: Rushing to class without breakfast, ordering fried chicken late at night, skipping lunch to lose weight — unhealthy eating is common among college students. Such habits may seem harmless now, but they often lead to stomach problems, weight gain and poor concentration in class. Our bodies are still growing, and a balanced diet is the fuel for both study and exercise. Therefore, we should eat three meals regularly, never leaving out breakfast, which provides energy for the whole morning. We had better choose more fresh vegetables and fruit instead of fast food, and stop ordering takeout several times a week. Good health begins on the plate.

writing.title: How to Deal with Stress
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on how college students should deal with stress. You should analyze the sources of stress and suggest effective ways to relieve it.
writing.promptZh: 分析大学生压力的来源，并提出缓解压力的有效方法。
outline: 第一段：现象——学业、就业等压力让不少学生焦虑
第二段：应对方法（运动、倾诉、合理目标、培养爱好）
第三段：总结——适度压力是动力，学会与压力共处
writing.model: Exams, job hunting and peer pressure make many college students feel anxious. A certain amount of stress is normal, but long-lasting stress harms both our health and our study. So learning to deal with it is a must. First, physical exercise is a proven stress killer; running or swimming helps the brain release chemicals that improve our mood. Second, talking with friends, parents or counselors keeps bad feelings from piling up inside. Third, we should set realistic goals and break big tasks into small steps, which makes pressure more manageable. Above all, remember that stress is not our enemy. Handled well, it can even push us forward.

expressions.zh: 被证实有效的减压方式

expressions.en: break big tasks into small steps

writing.title: On Saving Money as a College Student
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on whether college students should learn to save money. Give your reasons and practical suggestions.
writing.promptZh: 论述大学生是否应学会存钱，给出理由与实用建议。
outline: 第一段：现象——月光族在学生中不少见
第二段：存钱的意义（应对急用、体会父母辛劳、培养理财意识）与做法（记账、区分需要与想要）
第三段：总结——节约是一种成熟
writing.model: At the end of every month, quite a few students find their living allowance gone, a phenomenon jokingly called being the "moonlight clan". In my view, learning to save money is a necessary lesson for every college student. Saving is not about being mean. It prepares us for emergencies, such as buying a textbook or seeing a doctor, and it teaches us how hard our parents work for every yuan. Practically, we can keep a simple account book, or use an app, to see where money goes, and always ask ourselves whether we really need something before paying. Saving builds self-control, and self-control builds a better future.

writing.title: A Good Teacher-Student Relationship
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on what makes a good teacher-student relationship. You should explain its importance and how students can help build it.
writing.promptZh: 论述良好师生关系的重要性，以及学生可以为建立它做些什么。
outline: 第一段：良好师生关系促进学习效果与个人成长
第二段：学生的做法（尊重老师、主动提问、诚实反馈）
第三段：总结——师生互信，教学相长
writing.model: A good relationship between teachers and students benefits both sides. When we trust our teachers, we listen more carefully and dare to ask questions; when teachers understand us, they can teach in ways that truly suit us. As students, we can do much to build such a relationship. First, show basic respect: greet teachers, arrive on time and listen without interrupting. Second, be active in class and visit teachers after class when difficulties arise, since they are always willing to help. Third, give honest feedback instead of pretending to understand everything. Teaching and learning promote each other, and mutual trust is the bridge between them.

expressions.en: teaching and learning promote each other

writing.title: My Favorite Sport
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on your favorite sport. Describe the sport, explain why you like it and what you have gained from it.
writing.promptZh: 介绍你最喜欢的运动，说明喜欢它的原因以及从中获得的收获。
outline: 第一段：点明最喜欢的运动及接触它的契机
第二段：喜欢的原因（强身健体、团队合作、释放压力）
第三段：收获——坚持与协作精神伴随成长
writing.model: Among all kinds of sports, basketball is my favorite. I first touched a basketball in middle school, and since then it has become an important part of my life. I love it for several reasons. For one thing, running and jumping on the court keeps me strong and energetic. For another, basketball is a team sport: passing, screening and cheering for each other taught me the meaning of cooperation. Besides, an hour of playing washes away the tiredness of a whole day's study. From basketball I have learned that practice makes perfect and that a team is stronger than any single star. I will keep playing it for years to come.

writing.title: Behaving Well in Public Places
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on uncivilized behaviors in public places. Describe the problems, explain why good manners matter and call for action.
writing.promptZh: 描述公共场所的不文明行为，说明文明礼仪的重要性并发出倡议。
outline: 第一段：现象——大声喧哗、插队、乱扔垃圾等
第二段：文明举止的意义（体现个人素养、方便他人、展示社会风貌）
第三段：号召——从细节做起，做文明公民
writing.model: Loud phone calls in the library, cutting in line at the canteen and rubbish left on the playground — uncivilized behaviors still appear in public places from time to time. Some people think these are small things, but good manners are never small. They show our personal qualities and make public life comfortable for everyone. Queueing fairly saves time for all; keeping our voice down respects others' peace. As college students, we are supposed to set a good example. Let us start from small things: throw rubbish into the bin, speak softly in public and offer our seats to those in need. A civilized society is built by every polite citizen.

writing.title: How to Improve Spoken English
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on how to improve spoken English. You should analyze why many students speak poorly and offer practical suggestions.
writing.promptZh: 分析许多学生口语差的原因，并提出提高英语口语的实用建议。
outline: 第一段：现象——学生笔试成绩好却开不了口（哑巴英语）
第二段：原因（怕犯错、缺乏练习）与建议（大声朗读、找语伴、利用APP、大胆开口）
第三段：总结——开口是学好口语的第一步
writing.model: Many students can get high marks in written English tests but freeze up when asked to speak. This "mute English" results mainly from fear of making mistakes and lack of practice. To improve our spoken English, we should first change our attitude: mistakes are a necessary step in learning, and nobody laughs at a brave speaker. Then comes daily practice. Reading aloud every morning trains our tongue, talking with a language partner gives us real conversation, and English apps provide chances to practice anytime. Most importantly, seize every opportunity to open our mouth, in class, at English corners or with foreign friends. Practice makes perfect, especially for speaking.

writing.title: The Importance of Having a Hobby
writing.prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 10 minutes to write a short essay of about 80-100 words on the importance of having a hobby. Explain its benefits and encourage students to develop one.
writing.promptZh: 论述拥有兴趣爱好的重要性，说明其益处并鼓励大家培养爱好。
outline: 第一段：现象——很多学生除了学习没有爱好，生活单调
第二段：爱好的益处（放松身心、结交朋友、发现潜能）
第三段：号召——找到热爱，点亮大学生活
writing.model: When asked about their hobbies, some students answer that studying is all they do. A life without any hobby, however, is like a garden without flowers — dull and lifeless. Hobbies bring us many gifts. After hours of hard study, playing the guitar, painting or hiking helps our tired minds relax and recover. Hobbies also connect people: joining a club, we meet friends who share our interests and feel less lonely in a new city.
